newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude slightly firmer, Jul/Aug the focus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude slightly firmer, Jul/Aug the focus.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were slightly firmer Monday morning, with most focus on the July/August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spread, traders said.

August WTI/Cushing benchmark was around 10-15 cents higher at $18.95-19.05 a barrel, gaining on technical factors and nervous positioning on the tensions between Iraq and the U.N. over weapons inspections.
July WTI/Cushing cash was pegged some 25-30 cents weaker than August, with last deals recorded at -27 cents.
Spreads for the July domestic grades were steady to slightly firmer, with deals recorded for a rallying Midland/WTI market at -25 cents, traders said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked around steady, with deals seen at WTI/Cushing -2 cents and at flat to the marker.
WTI/Cushing Postings was talked at a wide $1.65-75, within the ranges pegged on Friday.
Sour barrels were also steady from Friday at discounts of 95 cents to $1.05 to the benchmark, and Eugene Island around a $1.70 under level.
